title: Pricing & Commitments Triage: Enterprise Intake SLA and Data Checklist
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Purpose:
This ticket defines a pragmatic intake and triage playbook for enterprise pricing and billing requests that are non-bug (commitments, invoicing mapping, cost allocation, marketplace SKUs, exception requests). The goal is to shorten time-to-decision, standardize data collection for Finance/Legal/TPMs, and establish SLAs for response/decision and handoff to Eng/Legal/Finance.

Scope:
- Inbound requests from Customer Success, Sales, or Support that require pricing/commitment changes, invoice mapping exceptions, marketplace listing adjustments, or special cost allocation rules.
- Not included: product defects, runtime outages, or model safety incidents (those go to incident routing).

Intake workflow (high level):
1) Intake: CS/Sales submits a Pricing Intake form (Confluence link below). PM performs immediate triage within 48 business hours.
2) Data completeness check: PM requests missing fields using a templated email. SLA: 72 business hours to reach full data set.
3) Qualification: PM marks request as Eligible / Needs Legal / Needs Finance / Not Feasible. SLA: 5 business days for initial qualification.
4) Decision & Routing: If Eligible -> route to Engineering & Finance for implementation estimate and invoice mapping. If Needs Legal -> Legal review k=72h. If Needs Finance -> Finance mapping + cost allocation runbook.
5) Implementation: Eng/Platform builds required config or backend mapping (estimate assigned).
6) Verification & Close: QA of invoice snapshots and customer confirmation, then close and update knowledge base.

Data checklist (fields PM must collect before routing):
- Customer name and Redwood account id
- Commitment identifier (contract number) and signed commitment amount (USD/month or tokens/month)
- Billing cadence and expected start date
- Target marketplace SKU or marketplace listing change details (if applicable)
- Desired invoice mapping (line item names, tax treatment, currency) or example invoice PDF
- Finance contact (name, email) and Legal contact (if complex terms)
- Customer justification and criticality (business reason, go-live date)
- Any data residency/regulatory constraints (VPC/on-prem, export controls)
- Existing ticket links (sales proposal, contract redlines, support threads)

Decision heuristics (how PM decides routing):
- Simple mapping (invoice label change, SKU rename) -> Finance + Ops with low engineering effort
- Commitment change that affects billing engine or committed capacity -> Finance + Eng + Legal review
- Any change that affects revenue recognition or contract terms -> Legal mandatory
- Marketplace listing or SKU-level billing -> Marketplace engineering + Finance

Escalation & SLA targets (target times from intake submission):
- Acknowledge: 24 business hours
- Initial triage and completeness check: 48–72 business hours
- Qualification decision: 5 business days
- Legal referral decision: 72 business hours after referral
- Engineering estimate assigned: 7 business days if scoped
- Final decision communicated to customer: 10 business days for non-complex requests

Telemetry & audit requirements:
- Every decision must include a single-line rationale stored in the ticket
- Attachment of sample invoice or mapping spec is required for Finance handoff
- Track time spent by role (PM, Finance, Legal, Eng) for future SLAs

Operational playbook notes:
- Use templated intake form to reduce back-and-forth (link below).
- For high-value customers (> $250k ARR) initiate a weekly standing sync until case closed.
- Maintain a small library of common invoice mapping patterns and marketplace SKU templates to speed implementation.

Related artifacts and links:
- Intake form (template): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Pricing+Intake+Form
- Finance mapping spec (living doc): https://docs.redwood.ai/finance/mapping-guidelines
- Marketplace billing runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Marketplace/Billing+Mappings
- Example implementation PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-pr-templates/blob/main/pricing-mapping.md
acceptance_criteria:
- PM can close ticket only after required checklist items are attached.
- Finance confirms invoice mapping on a sample invoice within 5 business days of handoff.
- Legal sign-off recorded on tickets which changed contract terms or revenue recognition.
- Engineering prioritization or backlog placement documented with estimate and release target.
- SLA metrics captured in ticket metadata for at least 30 closed requests before finalizing SLA thresholds.
deliverables:
- Templated intake form published and linked from CS/Sales playbooks.
- Standard response templates for common outcomes (Approved, Needs Legal, Needs Finance, Not Feasible).
- A short internal runbook (1-page) for Finance to interpret incoming mapping specs.
- Dashboard tiles in Redwood Console showing open pricing requests and SLA breach rates.
comments: 2025-02-10 Alyssa Chen: Created ticket. Drafted initial intake workflow after a week of customer-facing asks that lacked consistent data. Goal: reduce back-and-forth and improve first-contact resolution.

2025-02-14 Marco Ruiz: Reviewed draft checklist; suggested adding explicit marketplace SKU field and example invoice requirement. Added estimate 5 points for initial implementation (templates + playbook).

2025-02-18 Finance (S. Patel): Finance requested that we include payment terms and revenue recognition impact fields; flagged that some mappings require GL code alignment. Marked as Needs Finance for those items.

2025-02-21 Legal (K. Oduro): Legal noted that any change that modifies contract consideration must include redlines and effective date; recommended mandatory Legal review trigger for revenue recognition changes.
2025-02-25 PM update: Incorporated Finance and Legal feedback. Prepared intake form and two response templates. Next: publish Confluence template and notify CS ops channel.

2025-02-28 Eng (R. Gupta): Implementation note: invoice mapping changes will require a small mappings-table migration and a scheduled deploy. Estimated 3 dev days plus QA. Tagged for runtime-1.18 backlog planning.
